San Jose weighs strict self-checkout rules to combat retail theft and tax revenue loss.
Evidence: $400K lost revenue, 1:3 staff ratios, union petitions
#Aletheia #Retail

San Jose officials propose capping items and mandating staff ratios at self-checkouts to protect workers and recover lost sales tax revenue.

Resulting Judgement: (-0.45, -0.55) — Lesser Evil

Regulatory burdens are shifted onto retailers under the guise of worker safety and tax recovery.

- San Jose Officials: FAIL (-0.45, -0.55) — Blames technology for theft.

San Jose is considering ordinances requiring a 1:3 staff-to-kiosk ratio and 15-item limits at self-checkouts to address $400,000 in annual retail theft losses.

The Poison:
Punishing automated efficiency with rigid mandates raises consumer prices without stopping organized shoplifting.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing WHERE (the physical checkout station) with HOW (societal economic strain), treating automation as the culprit of crime.

Social Physics Analysis:
The city runs a Smart Selfish Maneuver. It creates a manufactured crisis around retail automation, projecting blame onto grocers to justify regulatory overreach while avoiding systemic economic fixes.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. Bureaucratic intervention worsens operational friction.

The Unavoidable Truth: Retail theft creates genuine financial strain for local municipalities and storefronts.

The Unavoidable Lie: Imposing rigid checkout staffing ratios solves systemic theft and revenue shortfalls.
